newsitem.title: CHINA: China adds Jupiter moon to list of science firsts.
newsitem.headline: China adds Jupiter moon to list of science firsts.

text.p: China, inventor of the magnetic compass and gunpowder, has added a moon of the planet Jupiter to its list of scientific firsts by claiming that an eagle-eyed ancient spied the satellite nearly 2,000 years before Galileo.

"Findings in an ancient book on astrology show that Gan De, a noted Chinese astronomer of the Warring States period (475-221 BC), viewed Jupiter with the naked eye and saw one of its 16 moons in 364 BC," the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.

Although Gan De's original notes had been lost, researchers at the Chinese Academy of Sciences had found another tome dating from the Tang Dynasty (618-907) containing Gan's apparent descriptions of Jupiter and its third moon, Xinhua said.

"It's possible that ancient people could find Jupiter's (third) satellite if people's eyesight, time and other factors were suited to such observation," Xinhua quoted an official at the academy as saying.
The claim, if true, would usurp that of 17th century Italian astronomer Galileo, who is credited with discovering with a telescope in 1609 that Jupiter had moons.
China frequently makes claims to have invented things commonly thought to be Western innovations, such as forks and spoons, spaghetti and pizza.
